purpose: Machine-readable source map for the Blackwell warp-specialization study. It connects every teaching claim and compiler-pipeline checkpoint to frozen source symbols, tests, and case-matrix entries.

evidence_kind.fact: Directly established by source code, pass registration, test fixture, or FileCheck at the frozen commit.
evidence_kind.inference: Reasoned expectation, chiefly PTX/SASS interpretation or performance implication; not established by an SM103 runtime measurement.

support_level.core: Part of the default Blackwell compiler pipeline.
support_level.tested: Covered by focused MLIR or Python tests at this commit.
support_level.heuristic: Implemented and tested, but policy is deliberately heuristic rather than a semantic guarantee.
support_level.experimental: Implemented with meaningful coverage but subject to explicit restrictions, FIXMEs, or a narrow recognized shape.
support_level.limited: Only a negative/no-op contract or a compile-only structural claim is established.

interpretation.symbol_note: Symbols name Python functions/classes, C++ functions/classes, pass factories, MLIR test functions, or kernel definitions.

knowledge_points.title: warp_specialize is a loop hint, not a promise that a partition will be formed
knowledge_points.summary: The frontend emits tt.warp_specialize on scf.for. Eligibility and profitable partition formation are decided later; a marked loop can remain unspecialized.

tests.checks: Marked loop produces no warp-specialize op without eligible descriptor memory operations.

limitations: At this snapshot automatic eligibility requires recognized descriptor load/store roots; a generic async-copy-only loop does not establish autoWS support.

knowledge_points.title: Default autoWS is in the Blackwell compiler branch
knowledge_points.summary: compiler.py invokes automatic warp specialization in the capability // 10 >= 10 branch, after latency assignment/scheduling and before pipeline materialization.

tests.checks: Blackwell E2E compile/run fixture with TMA requirements.

limitations: All proposed evidence is sm103 compile-only and makes no runtime-equivalence claim.

knowledge_points.title: PartitionScheduling turns dataflow roots into a fixed-point partition assignment
knowledge_points.summary: A graph is built over loop operations. Descriptor loads/stores, TMEM loads, TCGen5 MMA/scaled MMA, and manual data tags seed data partitions; merge constraints and heuristics run to a fixed point, partitions propagate, cheap/view operations may be duplicated, and temporary IDs are serialized.
limitations: Partition boundaries are policy, not ABI; heuristic changes can alter the exact number or membership of partitions.

knowledge_points.title: PartitionLoops materializes independent warp-group programs
knowledge_points.summary: The pass recursively clones for/if/reduce and ordinary operations into nvws.warp_group regions, remaps loop-carried values and captures, and rejects unresolved cross-partition SSA dependencies.
limitations: Correctness depends on preceding ARef/TMEM-ARef passes eliminating non-representable cross-partition SSA edges.

knowledge_points.title: InsertAref makes producer-consumer hand-off explicit
knowledge_points.summary: Cross-partition tensor, scalar, and shared-memory values are wrapped in ARef create/put/get protocol operations. Tensor-descriptor loads become NVWS descriptor loads writing ARef-owned shared storage; consumer exits are placed after a suitable post-dominator.

sources.role: Convert descriptor load to ARef-aware producer.

tests.checks: One value with register and shared uses.

limitations: ARef is an intermediate compiler protocol; its operation names are not stable runtime ABI.

knowledge_points.title: InsertTmemAref tracks TMEM ownership over async-token DAGs
knowledge_points.summary: The pass builds a TMEM access DAG, detects producer/consumer partitioning, inserts ownership ARefs and stage annotations, and contains a loop-scheduler workaround. The implementation models ping-pong hand-off and caps the scheme at two groups.

sources.role: Async token and TMEM access graph.
Repair schedule information around the transformed loop.

limitations: Ping-pong ownership supports at most two participating groups in this implementation.
Scaled TMEM flows have targeted special handling rather than a general proof for arbitrary graphs.

knowledge_points.title: LowerAref turns ownership into empty/full barrier protocols and multibuffering
knowledge_points.summary: ARefs lower to barrier allocation, wait/arrive operations, concrete TMA loads, and shared/TMEM stage buffers. numStages controls multibuffering; compatible ARefs can be combined.

sources.role: Stage buffers and reduce redundant protocols.

limitations: Source comments acknowledge that some generated synchronization can expose less-than-ideal parallelism; structural correctness does not imply optimal overlap.

knowledge_points.title: LowerWarpGroup establishes the stable ttg.warp_specialize boundary
knowledge_points.summary: nvws.warp_group regions become ttg.warp_specialize partitions. The first group becomes the default region only when its warp count equals the module default; otherwise an empty default is created.

knowledge_points.title: HoistTmemStore removes safe persistent-loop TMEM clears
knowledge_points.summary: The pass recognizes TMEM allocation/zero-store/MMAv5 patterns under WS loops and can fold the clear into allocation or hoist allocation. Removal is guarded by useD=false and matching execution/trip behavior or proof the loop executes at least once.
limitations: This is a narrow pattern optimization; failure to match should preserve correctness but can retain synchronization and clearing cost.

knowledge_points.title: OptimizePartitionWarps shrinks worker groups with target-specific heuristics
knowledge_points.summary: Each partition is extracted and relayouted at candidate warp counts. The estimate uses twice the largest tensor i32-register footprint, a 65536-register SM budget, minimum 2 warps for TMA loads, minimum 4 for TMEM operations, and target register requests of 88 with tensor computation or 24 otherwise.

sources.role: Isolate and recompile a partition at alternate warp counts.

limitations: The register estimate is not ptxas occupancy analysis and does not predict runtime speedup.
Exact worker counts may change when layouts or heuristics evolve.

knowledge_points.title: AllocateWarpGroups gives worker partitions physical warp IDs and register budgets
knowledge_points.summary: All WS operations are padded to the kernel maximum number of extra four-warp groups. Larger groups receive lower IDs, total-num-warps is recorded, requested registers are rounded in eight-register units, and the remaining budget is assigned to the default region. Assert/print/instrumented regions retain a minimum of 32 registers.
limitations: The source retains a FIXME about four-warp alignment for TMEM-related allocation; treat exact group placement as implementation detail.

knowledge_points.title: ConvertWarpSpecializeToLLVM lowers WS to a persistent worker state machine
knowledge_points.summary: Warp IDs split the default path from worker paths. Worker warp groups repeatedly read shared state, switch to a partition body, synchronize, and return to the switch loop until an exit state. Captures are packed through shared memory; relative warp IDs and NVVM setmaxregister operations are materialized.

sources.role: Shared-state switch loop, capture storage, and partition CFG.

tests.checks: Captures, relative IDs, and arbitrary control flow.

limitations: PTX and especially SASS spellings are toolchain-dependent; the stable claim is the LLVM/NVVM control-flow and intrinsic structure.

knowledge_points.title: WS consumes a finite named-barrier budget
knowledge_points.summary: The common lowering supports at most 16 named barriers. One is reserved for the default region and one for the switch loop, leaving at most 14 partition barriers; a single-warp participant can use warp sync instead of a CTA named barrier.
limitations: Complex kernels can fail or require partition merging before reaching this limit; the budget is a hard implementation constraint, not a performance guideline.

knowledge_points.title: Correctness requires separate proxy and TMEM dependency analyses
knowledge_points.summary: ProxyFenceInsertion orders writes/reads crossing generic, async, TMA, TMEM, CTA, and cluster proxies. TMemBarrierInsertion separately analyzes overlap among TMEM alloc/load/store/MMA/copy accesses. These passes run before LLVM lowering.

tests.symbol: async, TMA, TMEM, cluster, and 2CTA fixtures

tests.checks: Required TMEM barrier placement and non-overlap cases.

limitations: ARef barriers express producer-consumer ownership; proxy/TMEM passes solve additional memory-model hazards and are not interchangeable with ARef synchronization.

knowledge_points.title: Blackwell MMA lowers through TCGen05 and TMEM
knowledge_points.summary: MMAv5 conversion constructs TCGen05 instruction descriptors, emits ordinary or scaled MMA, and commits completion to an mbarrier. Accumulators and operand staging use TMEM allocation/load/store/copy operations lowered to tcgen05 forms.

tests.checks: TMEM allocation under WS and captures.

limitations: TCGen05 is the compute substrate, not by itself evidence of automatic warp specialization; the IR must also contain the WS structure.

knowledge_points.title: Scaled MMA/block-scale is wired into partitioning and TCGen05 lowering
knowledge_points.summary: TCGen5MMAScaledOp is a partition root, scale operands may arrive through TMA/TMEM, and MMAv5 conversion emits FP8/FP4 block-scale descriptors and TCGen05 block-scale variants.

sources.role: Scale descriptor and scaled MMA lowering.
Frontend tl.dot_scaled example, not an autoWS proof by itself.

tests.checks: Partition assignment with register/TMA scale sources.

limitations: Focused tests cover selected layouts/types and descriptor scale paths; this is not evidence that every tl.dot_scaled combination auto-specializes.

knowledge_points.title: Two-CTA MMAv5 adds cluster-scoped synchronization to WS
knowledge_points.summary: Cluster analysis identifies distributed multi-CTA and cross-CTA commit dependencies. A cluster mbarrier allocator reserves two 16-byte slots plus a counter; initialization and use alternate slot/parity via a modulo-4 state and make all warps participate through synthetic WS when necessary.

sources.role: Allocate two cluster mbarrier slots and module attributes.
Initialization, modulo-4 parity protocol, and all-warp synchronization.

tests.checks: Cluster barrier lowering, relaxed form, and slot reuse inside WS.

limitations: Compile-only evidence validates IR/PTX structure, not launch viability, cluster residency, or speedup on an SM103 device.

knowledge_points.title: Repository coverage extends beyond one dense GEMM
knowledge_points.summary: Focused and end-to-end fixtures cover TMA GEMM, mixed TMA plus ordinary async copy, nested persistent GEMM, attention forward/persistent attention, grouped GEMM, scaled MMA, TMEM ownership, registers, and two-CTA cluster lowering.

tests.checks: Mixed load paths and grouped GEMM.

limitations: Breadth of fixtures is not the same as broad production maturity; many cases are focused MLIR tests with exact recognized shapes.

knowledge_points.title: Maturity is strongest in compiler structure, weaker in generality and performance proof
knowledge_points.summary: The default Blackwell pipeline, focused tests, Python integration fixtures, and tutorials demonstrate a coherent end-to-end implementation. Eligibility is narrow, several policies are heuristic, TMEM/cluster/scaled paths contain explicit restrictions, and no SM103 runtime measurement is available in this study. The defensible rating is production-oriented compiler machinery with experimental automatic-policy breadth.
limitations: Do not translate this assessment into a universal performance or stability guarantee.
SM103 SASS and runtime measurements remain deferred until suitable hardware/tool access is available.
